author: Golden Gate Media
title: California unlocks billions in student savings with CalKIDS-but many haven't claimed it
text:
11 hours ago In Sacramento, Gavin Newsom is using Tax Day to spotlight what he says is an overlooked opportunity for families to secure free money for their children’s futures. State leaders are urging Californians to sign up for CalKIDS, the nation’s largest state-led college savings program, as billions in available funds remain unclaimed.
Photo by Edgar Cedillo on Unsplash The program automatically deposits $100 into accounts for every child born in California on or after July 1, 2023, with an additional $25 available when families register online. Children born between July 2022 and June 2023 also qualify. For low-income public school students, the benefit grows significantly, with $500 automatic deposits available to help jumpstart college savings.
“Every child deserves a strong start. On Tax Day, we’re reminding Californians that help is already available – and it only takes a few minutes to claim it,” said Governor Gavin Newsom.
First Partner Jennifer Siebel Newsom emphasized the long-term vision behind the initiative. “California is committed to giving every child the best start in life. CalKIDS helps families build a future from day one so we can invest in our children’s full potential. There is no better time to start saving for the future than today!”
Launched in 2022, CalKIDS has already created more than 5.6 million accounts, with over $2.3 billion set aside. Yet only about 880,000 accounts have been claimed so far, highlighting a significant gap between eligibility and participation. The program, administered by the State Treasurer’s Office, has distributed $82.2 million to support 151,000 students currently attending school.
